research_notes: JV announced Aug 2024 between China's Ganfeng Lithium (via subsidiary Ganfeng LiEnergy) and Ankara-based Turkish battery maker Yiğit Akü. Total investment ~USD 500m; planned annual capacity 5 GWh of lithium battery cells plus pack assembly. The plant is a genuine CELL manufacturer: sources specify production of prismatic cells in 100Ah, 280Ah and 314Ah formats aimed primarily at the Turkish and international ESS market — these formats are near-universally LFP, so chemistry recorded as LFP (not explicitly stated in sources; solid-state / high-power / marine / aerospace cited only as future R&D directions). Location assumed Ankara (Yiğit Akü's base); exact site and coordinates not confirmed in sources, left null. Turkish-language sources gave a plan to be operational within 2025, but Ganfeng's own disclosure flagged the deal was still subject to Chinese regulatory approval with 'uncertainty' on timing/start-up, and no groundbreaking or construction milestone could be confirmed as of mid-2026 — hence status kept as 'announced' rather than under_construction, and start_year 2025 is a plan not a confirmed date. Cross-checked across CnEVPost, Caixin, electrive, Batteries International, Best Magazine and Türkiye Today; all trace to the same Aug 2024 announcement.

parent_company: CALB Group Co., Ltd. (China Aviation Lithium Battery)
research_notes: CALB's first European gigafactory, wholly owned (not a JV), in the Sines Industrial and Logistics Zone (ZILS), ~100 km south of Lisbon near the Port of Sines. ~45-hectare site with five production buildings covering electrode production, cell production, assembly and packaging — confirms it is a genuine cell manufacturer, not just pack assembly. Investment ~€2.065–2.07 billion; ~1,800 direct jobs; granted Project of National Interest (PIN) status and grid-access support; €350m Portuguese incentive package formalised Jan 2026. First announced via MoU in Nov 2022; definitive project announcement/groundbreaking Feb 2025; Phase 1 construction contract (€207.3m) awarded to Mota-Engil in May 2026 with a 22-month build to ~July 2028. Initial production targeted 2027 at ~15 GWh/yr, expanding to full nameplate ~45 GWh/yr by 2028 (nameplate_capacity_gwh set to eventual 45 GWh; ramp captured in capacity_by_year_json). Output targets both EV (automotive) and stationary ESS markets, mainly European customers, with a mix of NMC (NCM) and LFP chemistries. Cell format not confirmed by a source (CALB is known for prismatic cells but not sourced for this site) — left null. Precise plant coordinates not published in reviewed sources — left null rather than guess. Several trackers (electrive, CnEVPost, battery-news, evmagz) corroborate the 15→45 GWh figures and status; direct fetches of several pages returned HTTP 403, so details drawn from search summaries plus the ess-news primary article. Sources: ess-news.com (2026-01-28), chemxplore.com, portugalglobal.pt (Feb 2025), CnEVPost (2025-02-25).

Taiwan-based ProLogium's first manufacturing site outside Taiwan. Groundbreaking ceremony held 10 Feb 2026 (announced 2023 alongside President Macron); construction underway, so status = under_construction. Manufactures 4th-generation all-inorganic solid-state lithium-ceramic battery CELLS for the EV market, so is_cell_manufacturer = true. Total investment ~€5.2bn. Phased roadmap: Phase 1 completion 2028 with initial mass-production capacity 0.8 GWh/yr, ramping to 4 GWh/yr by 2030, and Phase 2 reaching 12 GWh/yr by 2032. Firm planned nameplate recorded as 12 GWh (ref year 2032); the site has stated long-term potential to scale up to 48 GWh/yr in later phases (not yet committed), hence nameplate kept at the firm 12 GWh figure. Located in the port of Dunkirk, Hauts-de-France, near the Gravelines nuclear plant for low-carbon power; precise coordinates not confirmed in sources, so lat/long left null. Cell format not confirmed by sources (ProLogium lithium-ceramic cells are typically pouch/laminated, but unconfirmed for this site), left null. Wholly owned by ProLogium, not a JV. Corroborated by ProLogium press release, GlobeNewswire, electrive, Battery-News, Evertiq and electriccarsreport.

parent_company: Xiamen Hithium Energy Storage Technology Co.
research_notes: Chinese ESS maker Hithium and the regional Government of Navarre (through development agency SODENA) signed an investment commitment / joint-venture agreement (~EUR400 million) to build a battery gigafactory in Navarre, Spain, in a ceremony attended by PM Pedro Sanchez. Status: announced only — site not yet legally finalised and permits from both Spanish and Chinese governments still pending; the leading candidate location is the former BSH plant at Esquiroz/Ezkirotz, ~5 km south of Pamplona (not confirmed, so coordinates left null). Spanish and company sources state the plant will house TWO industrial processes: BESS pack/system assembly AND battery cell manufacturing — hence is_cell_manufacturer = true. Chemistry inferred LFP and end-market ESS (stationary storage): Hithium is an LFP long-duration-storage specialist and the associated product shown is a 6.9 MWh BESS using a large 1,300 Ah prismatic cell (pv-magazine ES, 2026-06-10). Production targeted to start 2027. Phasing: phase 1 ~750 direct jobs, phase 2 adds ~300 (up to ~1,050 total). Won an EUR81 million grant under Spain's RENOVAL 2 scheme (IDAE/MITECO) announced late June 2026 — the largest of the battery awards. Nameplate GWh capacity NOT publicly disclosed by Hithium — left null rather than guessed. Confidence 0.6: multiple reputable news sources but early-stage, capacity/location/exact chemistry unconfirmed. Other sources: ess-news.com (2026-03-11), navarracapital.es (JV to begin manufacturing 2027), navarra.es official press release, pv-magazine.es (2026-03-10 and 2026-06-10).

Tiamat's first commercial sodium-ion (Na-ion) cell gigafactory, on a ~25 ha site in the ZAC Jules Verne 2 industrial estate at Boves, ~10 km south-east of Amiens (Somme, Hauts-de-France). Announced January 2024 (5 GWh full nameplate, ~€500m+ investment). Tiamat is a spin-out of the CNRS/RS2E network and manufactures Na-ion cells in the cylindrical 18650 format (basis for cell_format=cylindrical; not separately re-confirmed for this site). End markets are mixed: power tools/consumer, data-centre/ESS back-up, and eventually EV mobility.

STATUS: not yet operational. Implementation convention signed 7 May 2025; groundbreaking planned late 2025/early 2026, with the construction (chantier) reported by Courrier Picard as due to launch in 2026 — hence under_construction, but this is uncertain: as of mid-2026 funding was not fully secured (company still needed to raise a further ~€150-200m) and timelines have repeatedly slipped. If site works have not actually begun, status is better read as 'announced'.

CAPACITY: full nameplate 5 GWh phased to completion originally by 2029, later cited as 2030 (used as capacity_ref_year). First phase reported as 700 MWh (0.7 GWh), initially targeted 2025, delayed to 2026 (used in capacity_by_year_json and as start_year). A later (2025) report revised phase 1 to ~1.5 GWh by mid-2027 — a genuine conflict; the 0.7 GWh/2026 figure is more consistently cited. Full ramp to 500,000 cells/day by ~2030-2031.

COORDINATES are approximate (Boves commune / ZAC Jules Verne area), not a surveyed plant coordinate — treat as low precision. Other reputable sources: electrive.com (2024-01-12), pv-magazine.com (2024-01-19), ess-news.com (2024 & 2025), Amiens Métropole, usinenouvelle.com.

plant_name: Blue Solutions Quimper (Ergué-Gabéric / Odet mother plant)
research_notes: Blue Solutions' historic "mother plant" is at Ergué-Gabéric (Odet site) adjacent to Quimper, Brittany, France; the company also references the site as its Quimper Bretagne Occidentale facility. Operational since ~2011-2013, it is the only site worldwide mass-producing solid-state lithium-metal batteries using LMP (Lithium Metal Polymer) technology. Current output was ~500 MWh/yr on one line (a sister line of similar size sits in Boucherville/Montreal, Canada — that is a SEPARATE physical site, not double-counted here); a third line was being installed at Quimper to lift annual capacity toward ~1.5 GWh/yr. In Oct 2024 Blue Solutions raised funds for an additional 250 MW pilot line at Quimper to industrialise its new Gen4 solid-state battery. End market is mixed: LMP cells power Bluebus electric buses (EV) and stationary energy storage (ESS). NOTE: the widely cited 25 GWh "gigafactory" (≈€2.2bn, ~1,500 jobs by 2032) is a DIFFERENT, later project reportedly targeted at Alsace, not the Quimper site — do not attribute 25 GWh to Quimper. Capacity figures (0.5 GWh current, 1.5 GWh with third line) come from 2024 trade/regional sources and are somewhat approximate; exact ramp years are uncertain, hence moderate confidence. Coordinates left null (no sourced value). Cell format for LMP wound thin-film cells not clearly sourced, left null. Corroborating sources: electrive.com (2021-03-03), Bolloré press release (2024-05-17), sustainable-bus.com, quimper-bretagne-occidentale.bzh.

Giga Arctic (combined Gigafactory 1 & 2) at Mo Industrial Park, Mo i Rana. Board sanctioned construction June 2022 at 29 GWh nameplate on 24M Technologies SemiSolid LFP platform; ~USD 1.7bn capex; EU Innovation Fund EUR 100m grant (2023). Planned start of production 1H-2024. Company minimised European investment in 2023 to prioritise the US (Georgia) and completed the Giga Arctic building as a shell for a possible 'hot start'. In August 2024 FREYR put battery cell production at Mo i Rana on hold and cut staff, citing Chinese overcapacity/low prices; commercial production never reached full scale. FREYR rebranded to T1 Energy in 2024-25 and its US Georgia gigafactory was cancelled Feb 2025. A small Customer Qualification Plant (CQP) at Mo i Rana produced first SemiSolid cells in 2023 at pilot scale. Status recorded as under_construction (completed shell, production paused) rather than operational; some trackers may class it as paused/on-hold. Cell format not confirmed by a primary source, left null. Coordinates are approximate town/industrial-park level (Mo i Rana ~66.31N, 14.14E), not a surveyed site coordinate. 29 GWh is the full nameplate; no phased ramp materialised so capacity_by_year_json left null. Corroborating sources: greencarcongress.com (2022-06-30, 29 GWh / USD1.7bn / 24M SemiSolid LFP); energy-storage.news on minimising European investment; ess-news.com (2025-02-10) on Georgia cancellation.

plant_name: Saft/ACC Nersac Pilot Plant (Industrial Excellence Center)
research_notes: Nersac (Nouvelle-Aquitaine, near Angouleme) is a Li-ion battery CELL pilot / R&D line, not a commercial-scale gigafactory. Site was originally a Saft lithium-ion facility (Saft took full control 2013; ~60 MWh legacy capacity). It became the pilot plant for ACC (Automotive Cells Company), the JV between TotalEnergies/Saft, Stellantis and Mercedes-Benz. A ~EUR200m pilot line was launched (announced 2019-2020, pilot cell production from late 2021, formally inaugurated as the "Industrial Excellence Center"). It qualifies products/processes before scale-up at ACC's Billy-Berclau/Douvrin gigafactory. Chemistry is NMC (high-energy automotive). Reported pilot output ~150 MWh / 600 cells / 40 modules per day; treated here as ~0.15 GWh/yr nameplate but this is pilot-scale and the annualisation is uncertain, hence lower confidence. Because it is a JV site, operator set to ACC with a single row; partners in jv_partners (do not double-count under Saft, Stellantis or Mercedes). Cell format not confirmed (left null). Exact plant coordinates not sourced, left null (town of Nersac is ~45.65N, 0.05E). Sources: ACC facilities page (acc-emotion.com/facilities/nersac), MarkLines news on start of Nersac pilot production, electrive/TotalEnergies press on the pilot plant launch.

plant_name: Elinor Batteries Gigafactory (Eiktyr Industrial Park, Orkland)
research_notes: Norwegian battery start-up (founded 2023, launched Jan 2023) planning a giga-scale LFP cell plant at Eiktyr Industrial Park in Orkland municipality, Mid-Norway, near Trondheim. Backed primarily by green investment firm Valinor. Planned full nameplate ~40 GWh/yr by 2030, built in three modules (first module ~EUR 1bn investment). Cobalt/nickel-free LFP chemistry; marketed for EVs (~800,000 EVs equivalent) but also pursuing stationary storage (BESS) via a Stella Futura partnership targeting 5 GWh installed by 2030, hence end_market marked 'mixed'. August 2024 technology/manufacturing partnership signed with Chinese firm Morlus Technology (technology & plant-construction expertise, not confirmed as an equity JV, so jv_partners left null). Status uncertain and conflicting across sources: a final investment decision was expected by 2025 and first-module production was originally targeted for Q2/mid-2026, but more recent sources say construction is scheduled to begin in 2026 with production commencing ~2028. No confirmation that FID has been taken or ground broken as of mid-2026, so classified as 'announced' rather than under_construction. start_year left null due to the 2026-vs-2028 conflict. Coordinates and cell format not confirmed by a source, left null. Capacity is annual GWh/yr at full nameplate; no reliably sourced year-by-year ramp, so capacity_by_year_json left null. Sources: valinor.no investments page; elinorbatteries.com; Green Car Congress (2023-01-13); electrive (2023-01-25); Businesswire 'Breakthrough for Nordic Battery Initiative' (2024-08-28); battery-tech.net; energyindustryreview.com.

chemistry: LFP (high-power lithium-ion capacitor hybrid, sawdust-derived activated carbon)
research_notes: Beyonder AS (founded 2016, HQ Sandnes, Norway) operates a "Battery Center" at Forus, near Stavanger/Sandnes, for R&D, qualification testing and PILOT cell production — not a full-scale gigafactory. The Norway site does manufacture cells (LFP / lithium-ion capacitor high-power chemistry using sawdust-derived super-activated carbon), so is_cell_manufacturer=true, but only at pilot scale. The frequently quoted "up to 5 GWh" and "2.4 GWh secured for qualified product" figures refer to capacity via EXTERNAL manufacturing partners (Farasis Energy frame agreement in China; Leclanché MoU for large-scale production in Germany), NOT a Norwegian plant — hence nameplate_capacity_gwh left null to avoid attributing partner capacity to this site. Product branded "BePowered" for maritime, mobility, grid and industrial (mixed end market); recent MoUs with Corvus Energy (maritime, Mar 2026) and Hitachi Energy (grid). Cell_format recorded as cylindrical based on Beyonder's historic 21700-style cylindrical cells but not firmly re-confirmed for current pilot line — treat with caution. Company has faced financial strain (reported need for ~NOK 100m and a major contract; workforce ~42 in Jan 2025). Status set operational because the pilot line and company are active as of 2026; no dedicated commercial cell plant confirmed in Norway. Coordinates left null (not verified). Sources: beyonder.no/facilities, businessnorway.com, investinrogaland.com, farasis-energy.com, leclanche.com, bw-group.com (Corvus MoU).

parent_company: Consortium of family offices led by ABACON Capital and SALVIA (acquired out of insolvency, July 2025)
research_notes:
Customcells' Itzehoe location is the company's headquarters and technology cluster / R&D and small-series cell production site (not a gigafactory-scale plant). It develops and manufactures application-specific lithium-ion cells in prototype and small-series volumes, including silicon-anode high-performance cells (notably for Lilium eVTOL aircraft), plus aviation, marine, automotive and other custom applications, in various formats (pouch/cylindrical). It is a genuine cell manufacturer, so is_cell_manufacturer=true.

No gigafactory-scale annual nameplate GWh figure is sourced for Itzehoe; capacity fields left null. A ~1 GWh cylindrical pilot line was associated with the separate Tübingen pilot facility (with €8m Baden-Württemberg funding), and Tübingen has since been closed and will not reopen. Cellforce (silicon-anode, ~20 GWh planned, JV with Porsche) is a distinct entity/site near Tübingen, not this Itzehoe location, so no jv_partners recorded here.

Status timeline: Customcells filed for insolvency for key operating entities on 30 April 2025 (triggered by the collapse of its largest customer Lilium). Insolvency proceedings opened 1 July 2025; a consortium of family offices led by ABACON and SALVIA acquired the core business (agreement completed ~2 July 2025). Operations at Itzehoe continue largely unchanged with ~80% of local jobs retained; R&D and cell production for existing customers continue. Marked status=operational. A December 2025 electrive report notes a refocused strategy under new ownership. Coordinates left null (no precisely sourced plant coordinates found; site is in Itzehoe, Schleswig-Holstein, near the Fraunhofer ISIT technology cluster). Sources: electrive (2025-07-03 fresh-start; 2025-04-30 insolvency; 2021 capacity/Itzehoe role), chemeurope, ess-news, battery-news, glademichelwirtz.

parent_company: CustomCells Holding GmbH (Abacon-led consortium following 2025 insolvency restructuring)
research_notes: CUSTOMCELLS Tübingen GmbH, Jopestraße 14, 72072 Tübingen, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. This is a specialty / small-to-medium-series battery CELL manufacturing site — one of Europe's advanced production lines for custom lithium-ion pouch cells (per company site cct-batteries.com). It is a genuine cell manufacturer, so is_cell_manufacturer=true, but it is NOT a GWh-scale gigafactory; capacity is well below 1 GWh/yr and no confirmed nameplate GWh figure exists, so nameplate_capacity_gwh left null. In 2025 the site added a pilot production line for large-format 46mm cylindrical (round) cells under the state-funded "Roundabout" project (~EUR 8m Baden-Württemberg funding), hence cell_format='mixed' (pouch in series + cylindrical pilot). Chemistry is specialty high-performance Li-ion including silicon-anode work. End market historically mixed (specialty/e-mobility; largest customer was eVTOL maker Lilium, whose Oct-2024/Feb-2025 collapse triggered CustomCells' insolvency filing in April 2025 for its Itzehoe and Tübingen entities). An Abacon-led investor consortium took over key parts in July 2025, refocusing on high-performance e-mobility cells; Tübingen operations continue, so status='operational'. NOTE: do NOT confuse this Tübingen site with the separate Porsche/CustomCells JV Cellforce Group plant in Kirchentellinsfurt/Reutlingen (~1 GWh, up to 20 GWh planned) — that is a distinct physical site. Coordinates left null (street address confirmed but exact site geocoordinates not sourced). Sources: electrive.com (insolvency 2025-04-30; fresh start 2025-07-03), battery-news.de (round-cell pilot 2025-03-14), cct-batteries.com company site, cellforcegroup.com.

Battery CELL manufacturer: Blackstone Technology GmbH ran a lithium-ion cell line in Döbeln, Saxony, using its proprietary 3D-printing process for electrodes, primarily LFP chemistry (also pursued solid-state R&D). Pilot production began 2021 reaching ~50 MWh (0.05 GWh/yr) capacity by end-2021, with a stated goal of ~500 MWh (0.5 GWh/yr) in 2022 (capacity_by_year_json reflects this pilot ramp). The company acquired property and announced a multi-stage expansion to a preliminary peak of 5 GWh/yr (targeted ~2023-24) — recorded as nameplate_capacity_gwh, but this gigafactory scale-up was NEVER built. STATUS: the site is effectively defunct. Blackstone Technology GmbH filed for insolvency in June 2023; parent Blackstone Resources AG went bankrupt August 2024. As of 2024-2025 the insolvency administrator found no buyer for the whole Döbeln site and is selling assets piecemeal; ~84 creditors registered >€16m in claims. Chemnitz prosecutors investigated alleged subsidy fraud; Swiss FINMA cited capital-market transparency breaches. Status set to null because none of announced/under_construction/operational describes a closed/insolvent, dismantled plant — it was operational only at small pilot scale (2021-2023) before failing. Coordinates and cell format left null (not reliably sourced). Sources: electrive.com (2024-01-15, dismantling; 2023-06-29 bankruptcy; 2021-07-05 500 MWh goal), Blackstone Resources press release (2021-07-01 capacity tenfold), businesswire (2020-10-19 Döbeln location pick), evertiq/pressebox (5 GWh property acquisition), Wirtschaft in Sachsen (insolvency/creditors), de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackstone_Resources.

chemistry: mixed (Li-ion pouch; NMC, LFP, LTO, plus niobium-oxide and other PFAS-free electrode chemistries)
research_notes: Leclanché's Willstätt site (Baden-Württemberg, near Offenburg/Kehl) is an operational lithium-ion pouch-cell plant, described as the largest Li-ion pouch cell production facility in Europe, operating since 2012. Uses proprietary water-based, PFAS-free electrode/cell manufacturing. In Dec 2018 Leclanché announced tripling capacity to >3 million cells/yr (~1 GWh) by 2020; ~400,000 cells/yr reported in 2021. In November 2025 Leclanché and the EU's CINEA signed a €74.2 million grant agreement to expand the Willstätt site to 2 GWh capacity; the site is therefore OPERATIONAL today (~1 GWh nameplate) with a funded expansion toward the 2 GWh figure recorded here as the eventual nameplate. The €74.2M grant is conditional on Leclanché securing €141.3M co-financing by financial close (scheduled end-June 2026); project activities expected to commence January 2026. capacity_ref_year left null because sources do not state the year the 2 GWh nameplate is reached, and capacity_by_year_json left null (no phased figures published). Chemistry is mixed: pouch cells across NMC, LFP, LTO and newer niobium-oxide/PFAS-free chemistries. End markets are mixed: e-transport (buses, trucks, commercial/marine) and stationary energy storage. Coordinates are Willstätt municipality centre (town-level, not a verified factory address). source_date is the access date; the primary CINEA press release is dated November 2025 (company page returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool, so details are from the company release text surfaced via search and corroborating trade press: Battery-Tech Network, Battery Tech Association, MarkLines).

chemistry: LTO (lithium titanate); company later shifted to LFP
research_notes: Itzehoe is Liacon GmbH's registered HQ and R&D base (co-located with Fraunhofer ISIT, from which Liacon spun out) — NOT the company's volume cell-manufacturing site. Liacon's actual lithium-titanate (LTO) polymer cell production is at Ottendorf-Okrilla near Dresden (reported ~350 MWh/yr, >1 million cells/year; originally announced as up to 300 MWh/yr with production from H1 2019). Therefore is_cell_manufacturer set false for the Itzehoe physical site (HQ/R&D; at most pilot/small-series LTO work via Fraunhofer ISIT's FAB-SH line, not confirmed as commercial cell manufacturing at this address). Liacon GmbH was renamed/succeeded by TRION Battery GmbH (same commercial register entry, Amtsgericht Pinneberg HRB 15975 PI), which has shifted focus to LFP batteries and systems (12V LFP product launched 2023). Cell format inferred as pouch from 'lithium titanate polymer cells' description. No sourced nameplate capacity, start year, or coordinates specific to Itzehoe; all left null. Capacity/status figures found in reporting refer to the Ottendorf-Okrilla factory, not Itzehoe — that would be a separate physical site/row. Low confidence due to HQ-vs-plant ambiguity and sparse Itzehoe-specific data. Sources: battery-tech.net Liacon profile; greencarcongress.com (2019 BMBF cell-manufacturing launch); Oiger (2018) on the Saxony/Ottendorf-Okrilla factory; northdata TRION Battery GmbH / Liacon GmbH (same HRB 15975 PI).

jv_partners: Iberdrola, CIE Automotive, Enagas, EIT InnoEnergy, CIC energiGUNE
research_notes: Basque solid-state / lithium-metal battery initiative at the Alava Technology Park (Parque Tecnologico de Alava), Vitoria-Gasteiz (Minano), in the Marie Curie building near CIC energiGUNE. Backed by a consortium of Iberdrola, CIE Automotive, Enagas, EIT InnoEnergy and CIC energiGUNE; no single ultimate parent, so parent_company left null and stakeholders recorded in jv_partners. ~EUR700m planned investment, 800+ direct jobs. A ~4,500 sqm pilot/innovation line began construction in summer 2023, is operational and has produced first cells (initial 20Ah cells). In May 2026 Basquevolt launched a commercial lithium-metal cell, BQV400L (402 Wh/kg, 27 Ah, made in Spain, ~75% European components, HL3 safety cert). STATUS is nuanced: recorded as operational because the pilot line is manufacturing commercial cells now (July 2026), but the large-scale 10 GWh gigafactory is a 2027 target. Roadmap: ~1 GWh facility with cell production targeted for end-2025, scaling to 10 GWh nameplate by 2027 - captured in capacity_by_year_json; nameplate_capacity_gwh=10 is the eventual full figure (ref year 2027, still a target/announced scale, not yet installed). Cell format not confirmed from sources (lithium-metal cell, likely pouch) so left null. End market recorded as mixed: targeting EV plus stationary/ESS (developed a solid-state module for stationary storage with Bcare under the Iberdrola-led ASTRA-CC project, Jan 2026). is_cell_manufacturer=true (genuinely produces battery cells). Coordinates left null - no source gave exact decimals; site is the Alava Technology Park, Minano/Vitoria-Gasteiz. Confidence 0.6: status/capacity split between a running pilot line and an unbuilt 10 GWh target; figures from company and reputable trade press (basquevolt.com, electrive, Iberdrola, InnoEnergy).

Single physical site in the Teverola (Caserta, CE) industrial zone, Campania, Italy — Italy's/Southern Europe's first lithium cell gigafactory, run by FAAM, a subsidiary of Seri Industrial S.p.A. The site comprises two adjacent plants: Teverola 1, operational since 2021, produces lithium cells/modules/packs at ~0.35 GWh/yr (originally NMC lithium-ion). Teverola 2 is the gigafactory expansion under construction: 8 GWh/yr nameplate of high-efficiency LFP prismatic cells aimed at stationary storage (BESS/ESS). Investment reported ~EUR 505m total (EUR 150m SACE-guaranteed financing; ~EUR 200m spent by end-2025); equipment (incl. LEAD Intelligent Equipment end-of-line lines) being installed 2025, production start targeted 2026-2027 (Il Sole 24 Ore: by 2027). I chose status=under_construction and nameplate=8 GWh to reflect the defining Teverola 2 build; Teverola 1's 0.35 GWh operational line is a separate status and not summed here per the no-mixed-status rule. Chemistry recorded as LFP for Teverola 2 (site is mixed given Teverola 1's earlier NMC). Not a JV — the Eni/Seri stationary-battery JV concerns a separate Brindisi plant, not Teverola. Coordinates left null: only the address (Zona Industriale SS Appia 7-bis, 81030 Teverola CE) is confirmed; the nearby ~41.009,14.228 point refers to the Teverola CCGT power station, not the battery plant, so not used. Sources: FAAM/Seri Industrial, battery-news.de (2025-05-21), Il Sole 24 Ore, Batteries News (SACE financing).

UK battery start-up Volklec (founded/led by ex-Lotus boss Jim Farrell/team). Coventry operation is based at the UK Battery Industrialisation Centre (UKBIC) — a shared publicly-funded facility — where Volklec launched cell production in 2025 using UKBIC's existing 100MWh line to make a proven NMC 21700 cylindrical "energy cell" for e-mobility (e-bikes, scooters) and energy storage. An additional 1GWh line is to be installed by end of 2026 for a higher-power "power cell" (automotive, aerospace, marine, off-highway). The stated strategic roadmap is a dedicated 10GWh gigafactory (>£1bn / ~US$1.2bn investment, 1,000+ jobs by 2030). Technology comes via a licensing/knowledge-transfer partnership with Far East Battery (FEB) of China — this is a tech-transfer/licensing deal rather than a confirmed equity JV, so jv_partners should be read with that caveat. Status is genuinely mixed: small-scale production is underway at UKBIC (arguably operational at 0.1GWh), the 1GWh line is under construction, and the 10GWh dedicated gigafactory is only announced — recorded here as under_construction to reflect the active capacity ramp, with the phased ramp captured in capacity_by_year_json and full/eventual nameplate of 10GWh (ref 2030). No confirmed dedicated-site coordinates found (UKBIC is in Coventry); lat/long left null to avoid inventing. Nameplate/ramp figures from multiple trade-press reports of the Feb/Mar 2025 announcement; not independently verified by an official filing. Sources: bestmag.co.uk, E&T (eandt.theiet.org, 2025-02-27), electrive.com (2025-03-03), power-technology.com, batterytechassociation.org, volklec.com press release.

chemistry: lithium-ion, sodium-ion (mixed; high-power Li-ion and Na-ion)
research_notes: Long-established battery cell plant in Thurso, Caithness (Scottish Highlands) — operated for 20+ years, originally making cylindrical D cells for the UK MoD, then shifting to R&D and small-batch commercial cell manufacture. Under AMTE Power it produced small volumes (thousands of cells/month) of "Ultra Safe" and "Ultra Prime" high-power lithium-ion cells plus sodium-ion cells for specialist EV and long-duration storage; cited by trackers as ~100 MWh/year capacity, i.e. 0.1 GWh/yr (recorded for ref year 2023; single-tracker figure, moderate confidence). This is confirmed cell manufacturing (not pack/module assembly). AMTE Power PLC entered administration in December 2023; Eindhoven-based LionVolt completed acquisition of AMTE's Scottish business and assets, including the Thurso cell production line, in January 2024, transferring ~20 jobs and repurposing the line for LionVolt's 3D battery technology — so cell manufacturing continues (status = operational). A separate, larger 0.5 GWh "MegaFactory" was planned by AMTE in Dundee (Michelin Scotland Innovation Parc) but is a different site and did not proceed under AMTE. Precise plant coordinates not confirmed by a source, so left null (site is in/near Thurso, Caithness). cell_format recorded as cylindrical based on the plant's cylindrical-cell heritage/products — moderate confidence.

Britishvolt's planned lithium-ion EV cell gigafactory on the former coalyard/power-station site at Cambois, near Blyth, Northumberland (~250 acres, ~30km north of Newcastle). Planned nameplate ~30 GWh/yr built in three 10 GWh phases, with first production targeted around 2023-24 and full capacity by 2028; total project cost cited at £2.6bn-£3.8bn, up to ~3,000-8,000 jobs. Site announced Dec 2020, planning approved July 2021, enabling/groundwork construction began Sept 2021 but was paused in late 2022. Company collapsed into administration on 17 January 2023 (EY administrators) after failing to secure equity funding; the plant never produced any cells and was never operational. Assets later bought out of administration by Australia's Recharge Industries (Feb 2023) and the site subsequently sold (2024) for redevelopment (reportedly a data centre campus). Status recorded as under_construction to reflect the furthest stage reached under Britishvolt, but the project is effectively defunct/cancelled. Cell format not reliably sourced; chemistry reported as li-ion for automotive (NMC-class) - treat as indicative. No reliable precise site coordinates found, left null to avoid guessing. Capacity figure (30 GWh, 3x10 GWh) corroborated across multiple news sources.

NO EVIDENCE OF A NYOBOLT SITE IN SUNDERLAND — this candidate appears to be a seed-list error/conflation. Nyobolt is a University of Cambridge spin-out (founded 2019 by Prof. Dame Clare Grey and Dr Sai Shivareddy) making ultra-fast-charging Li-ion cells using a niobium/tungsten-oxide (XNO) anode. Its actual UK footprint is: (1) Cambridge HQ / cell-engineering base, and (2) a pilot manufacturing and anode-materials plant in Haverhill, Suffolk (Homefield Road), which came on stream ~2024-2025 with a small headcount (12 rising to ~40-70). Nyobolt has publicly discussed plans for a UK cell factory scaling ~1-2 GWh initially toward 15+ GWh by ~2035, but no site has been confirmed in Sunderland — and no capacity figure is tied to a Sunderland location. The Sunderland gigafactory in Nissan's supply chain belongs to AESC (Envision AESC), an unrelated Japanese-owned manufacturer (~15.8 GWh initial). Nyobolt IS a genuine cell manufacturer (hence is_cell_manufacturer=true), but the specific "Nyobolt Sunderland" plant does not exist as described. Recommend deleting this candidate or relabelling it to the Haverhill, Suffolk site. All quantitative fields left null; confidence 0.1. Sources: BusinessWire Series C release 2026-05-06; Suffolk News (Haverhill plant); electrive/battery-news (AESC = Sunderland operator).

ElevenEs opened Europe's first industrial LFP battery-cell facility in Subotica, Serbia (address Tolminska 35, 24000 Subotica) in April 2023, initially a pilot/pre-series line producing prismatic LFP cells shipped as A/B samples to EV (cars, buses, trucks) and energy-storage (ESS) customers — hence end_market "mixed". Company stated a target of 500 MWh (0.5 GWh) annual capacity in 2024 for this site; that figure is a target rather than confirmed achieved output, so confidence is moderate. Several outlets (etn.news) later described it as "fully operational". Key investor: EIT InnoEnergy (equity/support investor, not ultimate parent — parent_company left null as ElevenEs is an independent startup). Distinct, larger future gigafactories are planned but are separate sites and should NOT be merged with this row: "Giga-I" (8 GWh by 2026) and "Giga-II" (40 GWh by ~2027), for an ultimate ~48 GWh ambition. Coordinates left null — only a street address was sourced, not confirmed decimal coordinates (Subotica city is ~46.1N, 19.67E but not verified for the plant). announced_year ~2021 based on Oct-2021 PR Newswire/InnoEnergy investment announcement to build a Serbian gigafactory. Sources: balkangreenenergynews.com; electrive.com (2023-04-25); energy-storage.news; seenews.com; innoenergy.com.

Altris Sandviken, branded the "Ferrum" facility, is a CATHODE MATERIAL plant, NOT a battery cell manufacturing site — is_cell_manufacturer=false. Altris signed a deal with AB Sandvik Materials Technology to house its first industrial-scale facility (1,800 m2) at Sandvik's site in Sandviken, Sweden. It produces ~2,000 tonnes/year of Altris's proprietary Prussian White sodium-ion cathode material (Fennac), described as enough to enable ~1 GWh of sodium-ion batteries per year. That 1 GWh is a battery-equivalent figure for the cathode output, NOT cell nameplate capacity, so nameplate_capacity_gwh is left null to avoid mixing metrics. Announced May 2022; construction from spring 2022; first output early 2023 — treated as operational. Chemistry is sodium-ion (Prussian White cathode). Actual sodium-ion CELL production by Altris is targeted at a separate/later gigafactory, not this Sandviken cathode plant. Coordinates left null (facility is within Sandvik's Sandviken industrial site, ~60.6N 16.8E, but exact plant coords not confirmed). Sources: Green Car Congress (2022-05-10), InnoEnergy, Uppsala University, energy-storage.news, CleanTechnica — all consistent that Sandviken = cathode material, 2000 t/yr = 1 GWh-equivalent.

LOCATION DISCREPANCY: The candidate "Pomega Samsun" appears mislabelled. Every source (company site, energy-storage.news, ONE, ceenergynews, battery-tech.net) places Pomega's only Turkish battery cell gigafactory in the Polatlı Organised Industrial Zone, Ankara — NOT Samsun. No source found for any Pomega facility in Samsun; treat as the Polatlı/Ankara plant. This is Turkey's first private-sector LFP cell gigafactory: LiFePO4 prismatic cells, ~100,000 m2, groundbreaking 2022, commissioned/opened 2023, initial nameplate 3 GWh/yr with a stated roadmap to 6 GWh/yr. A 2025 partnership with US firm Our Next Energy (ONE) contracts Türkiye cell output rising from 2 GWh (2026) to 5 GWh (2027) — these are ONE-contracted volumes, not necessarily separate nameplate. Primarily LFP for stationary/utility-scale ESS. Kontrolmatik also runs a separate US plant in Walterboro, South Carolina (distinct site, not this row). Coordinates not confirmed from a source, left null. Confidence reduced mainly due to the Samsun/Ankara naming mismatch; plant existence and specs are well-sourced. Sources: tr.pomega.com/en/about-us; energy-storage.news LFP gigafactory Q4; one.ai ONE-Pomega partnership; ceenergynews.com; battery-tech.net.

plant_name: Ford-LG Kocaeli (Ford / LG Energy Solution / Koç Holding battery cell JV — cancelled)
jv_partners: Ford Motor Company, LG Energy Solution, Koç Holding
research_notes: CANCELLED PROJECT. Announced 21 Feb 2023 as a non-binding MOU between Ford, LG Energy Solution and Koç Holding to build a commercial-EV battery CELL plant — one of Europe's largest — with at least 25 GWh/yr capacity, expandable to up to 45 GWh/yr; groundbreaking planned 2023, production start targeted 2026. On 10 Nov 2023 Koç Holding revoked the MOU citing the slowing pace of EV adoption ("timing not appropriate for a battery cell investment"); the JV was scrapped and no cell plant was built. NOTE: the planned site was an organised industrial zone near ANKARA, not Kocaeli — the "Kocaeli" in the candidate name likely conflates it with Ford Otosan's existing Kocaeli/Yeniköy vehicle plant, which has a battery PACK/MODULE assembly line (not cell manufacturing). Status set to null because the project is cancelled and none of announced/under_construction/operational reflects a dead project. Capacity (25 GWh, ref year = planned 2026 start) is the announced figure only. Chemistry/cell format not disclosed (LG Energy Solution typically NMC pouch for EVs, unconfirmed). Sources: Ford Media (2023-02-21), KED Global (2023-11-12), Reuters/Yahoo Finance (2023-11-10), InsideEVs, Battery-News.
